name: Neo4j
tagline: The default property-graph database, with Cypher, a big ecosystem and a managed cloud.
description: Neo4j is the most widely deployed native property-graph database and the place where Cypher was born. It stores nodes and relationships with index-free adjacency, so multi-hop traversals stay fast as data grows, and it ships vector indexes, full-text search and a large graph-algorithms library (GDS). Since 2025 it has used calendar versioning (2026.x), with 5.26 kept as the long-term-support line, and Cypher 25 now covers most mandatory features of the ISO GQL standard. It is the safe, well-documented choice for most graph projects, though advanced clustering, security and hot backups sit in the commercial Enterprise edition and AuraDB.

pricing.notes: Community Edition is free under GPLv3. AuraDB has a free instance plus usage-based Professional and Business Critical tiers; Enterprise is sold by contract.

scale.notes: Primaries replicate full copies via Raft; secondaries scale reads. Sharding a single graph needs Enterprise features (composite databases / Infinigraph).

strengths: Cypher is the most widely known graph query language and now tracks ISO GQL closely
Index-free adjacency keeps deep traversals fast regardless of total graph size
Graph Data Science library ships 65+ production algorithms (PageRank, Louvain, node embeddings)
Native vector indexes make it a common GraphRAG backend alongside LLM frameworks
Largest graph ecosystem: Bloom, APOC, Kafka connector, drivers, training and talent pool
weaknesses: Clustering, RBAC, online backup and hot standby require the paid Enterprise edition
Every primary holds the full graph, so write throughput and size are bound by one machine
Bulk-loading and large analytical scans are slower than columnar or MPP graph engines
JVM memory tuning (heap vs page cache) matters a lot for stable latency
notIdealFor: Petabyte-scale graph analytics on a single graph
Heavy aggregation reporting better suited to a warehouse
